protocol: F-15J descended from 22,000 to 7,000 ft before reascending toward a planned 31,000 ft. Aircraft altitude and indicated cabin altitude were both 30,000 ft at symptoms. The source attributes loss of pressurization to the canopy-control handle.
outcome_window: Symptoms at altitude resolved during or after emergency descent. Follow-up duration is unavailable.
note: Heat sensation, heaviness and narrowed vision. The authors suspected hypoxia and mild bends. Observation followed recovery after descent.

protocol: Pressurization failure at 22,000 ft aircraft altitude produced a rapid cabin pressure change from the equivalent of 6,000 to 22,000 ft. Emergency landing followed.
outcome_window: Chest pain and exertional dyspnea within a few minutes after landing. Later follow-up is unavailable.
note: An aviation physician diagnosed pulmonary DCS. Chest imaging showed no pneumothorax or pleural effusion, and no subcutaneous emphysema was recorded. Recovery followed recompression at Etajima.

protocol: Aircraft altitude 33,000 ft. The pressure system fault changed equivalent cabin altitude from 10,000 ft to a reported range of 26,000–28,000 ft.
outcome_window: Limb pain was reported in the account of the landing. Exact symptom latency and follow-up duration are unavailable.
note: The aviation physician found no neurological abnormality, diagnosed Type I DCS and reported recovery following recompression. The text cites Kusano et al. after this vignette.

protocol: A 52-year-old transport pilot reported three days of scuba diving while on leave in Okinawa, followed by chamber training the next day. Right infraclavicular formication began at 22,000 ft and training was interrupted.
outcome_window: Symptoms improved rapidly after chamber descent. The authors give no timed follow-up.
note: Observation only after improvement and unremarkable blood gas, pulmonary-function and chest X-ray findings. Exact time from final dive to test and a definitive DCS diagnosis are unavailable. Membership in the 243-case aggregate is unverified.

protocol: Strenuous exercise in cold conditions the day before training. Left shoulder heaviness and sharp joint pain followed the 30,000-ft chamber flight.
outcome_window: After completion of the chamber flight. Symptom improvement during or after recompression is reported without a clock.
note: The aviation physician referred the participant to the naval Undersea Medical Laboratory. Symptoms improved after recompression. Membership in the 243-case aggregate and the exact onset relative to landing remain unverified.
